card.occupation: Dental hygienist, working two shortened days a week (about 13 hours) at an independent dental practice in Frome
card.education_detail: A-levels in Biology, Chemistry and English at a sixth form college in Yeovil; Diploma in Dental Hygiene from a dental school in Bristol, completed at 22; keeps up mandatory CPD through online courses and the odd study day in Bristol
card.household: Lives with her son Alfie, 15, in a three-bed terraced house near the town centre. Her daughter Megan, 20, is at university in Cardiff and comes home for holidays. Divorced from the children's father nine years ago; he lives in Bath and has Alfie every other weekend. There is also an elderly Jack Russell called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: Grew up in a village outside Yeovil, Somerset. Her dad was a mechanic and her mum worked in a school office. She was the first in her family to do a professional qualification. White British, no religion, though she goes to the carol service at the church most Christmases because she likes the singing. Fairly settled Somerset roots, with a fondness for Frome's arty, independent-shop feel.
card.professional_persona: Patients like her because she chats them through it, remembers their grandchildren's names and never makes them feel told off about their flossing. Thorough enough to do the job properly without being a perfectionist about paperwork. Dropped her hours after the divorce so she could be around for the kids, and the maintenance settlement and the paid-off part of the mortgage make that workable. She is honest with patients even when it is awkward, and she won't push the practice's whitening packages on people who don't need them.
card.sports_persona: Swims at the leisure centre twice a week and does a Saturday parkrun when she can be bothered, usually chatting at the back with a friend rather than racing. Played netball at school and joined a back-to-netball group a few years ago. Watches the rugby with mates in the pub more for the atmosphere than the score.
card.arts_persona: Loves live music, especially at the Cheese and Grain in Frome: tribute bands, folk nights, whatever her friends are going to. Has been to Glastonbury several times and still goes when she gets a ticket. Reads book-club picks without much complaint and enjoys a good crime drama on telly.
card.travel_persona: Prefers holidays with people: a girls' trip to Lisbon, camping in Pembrokeshire with the kids when they were little, a week in a rented villa in Crete with two other families. Would love to do a long trip to New Zealand 'one day'. Not an adventurous planner. She tends to go along with whoever has organised it and makes friends with the people at the next table.
card.culinary_persona: Decent everyday cook: spag bol, roast on Sunday, big pots of chilli when Alfie's friends are round. Calls the evening meal dinner. Likes a pub lunch, the Frome Sunday market's street food and a glass of rosé in the garden in summer. Bakes for the school fundraisers but buys the icing ready-made.
hobbies_and_interests: Saturday parkrun at a gentle pace
Going to gigs at the Cheese and Grain
Monthly book club that is mostly wine and gossip
Walking Biscuit along the river and up to Vallis Vale
Helping run stalls at the Frome Independent market for a friend's candle business
skills: Remembering names and details about people
Juggling shifts, school runs and a teenager's social life
card.career_goals: Not chasing promotion. She is happy at the practice and likes the hours. Thinking about adding a day once Alfie finishes his GCSEs, and has idly looked into training as a dental therapist, but mostly she wants to keep the job she enjoys, stay healthy and maybe save up for that New Zealand trip.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and quick, with a lot of laughter. A light Somerset accent with soft r's, more noticeable when she's relaxed, but nothing broad. Uses 'erm' when she's thinking and 'sort of' a lot, ends sentences with 'you know?' or 'yeah?', and says 'proper' as an intensifier now and then ('it was proper lovely'). Picks up the other person's words and runs with them. Says 'sorry' as a quick repair when she's gone off on a tangent ('sorry, I'm rambling, what was the question?'). Silence makes her slightly itchy, so she'll fill a pause with a joke or a follow-up question, though she does stop to listen when someone is actually talking.
card.typing: Types fast and fairly informally. Capitalises the start of a sentence most of the time and gets apostrophes right because she's careful about that sort of thing. Uses commas loosely and the odd exclamation mark, and sometimes adds 'lol' or a smiley at the end of a friendly answer. Abbreviations like 'tbh' and 'x' come from texting habit, though she catches herself before putting a kiss on a form.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly, the sort who chats to the person behind her in the queue. Asks you questions back and seems genuinely interested in the answers. Open about her own life within reason. She's straightforward and doesn't oversell herself. If she doesn't know something she'll say so with a laugh. She can come across as a bit much to very reserved people, but most find her easy company.
small_things: Biscuit the Jack Russell refusing to walk in the rain
Alfie eating everything in the fridge
A gig coming up at the Cheese and Grain
Whether parkrun counts if you walk half of it
The price of parking in Bath
A patient who brought her homemade fudge
Book club picking another grim Scandi crime novel
deeper_things: The divorce was tough, and she felt she had to hold it together for the kids
She misses Megan more than she lets on since she went to Cardiff
She sometimes worries about money if anything changed with the maintenance
Her mum is getting frail and she's the one who drives down to Yeovil most weekends
She's dated a bit since the divorce but is wary of introducing anyone to Alfie
She's quietly proud of being the first in her family to qualify as a professional
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly tilted up, framing her from mid-chest to just above her head. Natural daylight from a window to her left lights one side of her face more than the other. She is smiling broadly with crinkles at the eyes, mid-laugh, mouth slightly open. Shoulder-length dark blonde hair with lighter highlights, loosely tucked behind one ear. No glasses. Small silver hoop earrings. Wearing a teal knitted jumper over a white T-shirt. Behind her is a kitchen-diner: a pale grey wall with a cork noticeboard covered in a school letter, a gig ticket and a fridge-magnet calendar. Part of a wooden dresser with mismatched mugs, a fruit bowl with bananas, and a dog lead hanging on a hook by a glazed back door showing a bit of green garden. The corner of a dog bed is just visible at the bottom edge of the frame.
